newsitem.title: UK: Mowlem back in profit, says may float unit.
newsitem.headline: Mowlem back in profit, says may float unit.

text.p: John Mowlem & Co Plc, the building to management services group bounced back into profit in the first half of 1996 and raised the possibility of a partial flotation of one of its units to increase shareholder value.

Mowlem may float off part of the access products and services unit during 1997. Pretax profits for the six months ended June 30 were 5.3 million pounds ($8.32 million), swinging from a 32.0 million loss. But turnover dipped to 693 million pounds from 741 million. The company decided to pay a dividend of one pence after no payoput last year.
The group said in its interim statement that a partial float of the division was one option under consideration by the board and its financial advisers.
Mowlem said there were "substantial growth opportunities" available to the group, citing the access services, facilities management and environmental services businesses in particular.
It added that growth opportunities and good prospects for the group "are not reflected in the present value."
The 1996 peformance was assisted by recent restructuring and cost-cutting, said Mowlem. Further progress is seen feeding through in the second half. ($1=.6373 Pound)
